# Trader's Path — project memory for Claude Code

A bilingual (English master, Thai mirror) learning course for traders and investors, written as an **Obsidian vault** that also builds into a **static website** in `site/`. Owner: Souksavath (Laos/Thailand, UTC+7). Audience: motivated beginners with zero finance background, many reading in their second language.

## Layout
```
00 Home.md                      vault home (MOC)
00 Markets, Brokers & News/     Phase 0  (new, Oct 2026)
01 Foundations/ … 11 Capstone/  Phases 1–11
  "<N> <Phase> - Index.md"      generated by sync.py — don't edit by hand
  "<id> <Title>.md"             one note per lesson, EN + TH in one file
_System/                        Templates/ (learner templates EN+TH), Dashboards/ (.base), Flashcards/ (generated), Learning Toolkit, Roadmap, Style Guide (v2!), Lesson Template, Lesson Audit, Glossary (→ site glossary + tooltips), Disclaimer (→ site/disclaimer.html), Task Board (generated), Add-on Ideas, Claude Code Handoff
_assets/charts/                 generated SVG figures: <name>.en.svg / <name>.th.svg
_tools/curriculum.json          single source of truth for phases & lessons (ids, EN/TH titles, folders)
_tools/charts.py                SVG toolkit: SVG, CandleChart, candles_from_path, C (colours), tr(lang)
_tools/figures/pN.py            figure functions for phase N, registered with @fig → "pN-name"
_tools/make_figures.py          python3 _tools/make_figures.py [p0 p8 …]
_tools/sync.py                  creates missing folders/index/stub notes; regenerates Task Board
_tools/build.py                 vault → site/ (only status: done lessons are published)
_tools/upgrade_lesson.py        insert v2 blocks into an existing lesson without rewriting it (idempotent)
_tools/site_src/                page.html, home.html, style.css, app.js (search, glossary tooltips), calculator.html + calc.js (position-size tool)
site/                           generated website — never edit by hand (git-ignored; GitHub Actions builds it: .github/workflows/publish-site.yml, see _System/Publishing Guide)
```

## Commands
```bash
python3 _tools/make_figures.py p5     # regenerate one phase's figures (EN + TH)
python3 _tools/drills/make_drills.py  # regenerate chart-drill rounds (_tools/drills/drills.json) before building
python3 _tools/flashcards.py          # regenerate _System/Flashcards decks from the lessons' [!terms] boxes and [!check] questions
python3 _tools/qa/figure_check.py     # measure every figure's text in Chrome: overflow / overlap report (target: 0 issues)
python3 _tools/qa/fact_register.py    # regenerate _System/Fact Register.md (time-sensitive facts, re-check dates)
python3 _tools/qa/thai_check.py       # regenerate _System/Thai Review List.md (EN↔TH mirror check + lines for a native read)
python3 _tools/make_pdfs.py           # printable PDF per phase and language → site/pdf/ (needs Chrome; run before build.py)
python3 _tools/build.py               # sync + build the site (also regenerates Task Board)
open site/index.html                  # view
```
Python 3.10+, `pip install markdown` is the only dependency.

## Lesson format (read `_System/Style Guide.md` before writing anything)
- Frontmatter: `id`, `phase`, `status: stub|draft|done`, `level: v2` (once upgraded), `tags`.
- `%% EN %%` then English; `%% TH %%` then `---` and the Thai mirror. Same blocks, same order, same figures (`.en.svg` ↔ `.th.svg`).
- Callouts: mindset, eli5, terms, concept, analogy, walkthrough, example, market, caution, action, why, warning, practice, key, tip, note, check (folded `[!check]-`) with nested `> > [!answer]-`.
- Self-check questions are written `**Q1.**`, never `1.` (numbered lists break around nested answers).
- Quizzes in checkpoints use the ```quiz block format described in the Style Guide.
- Gold-standard examples to copy: **0.1, 0.3, 0.8** (new lessons) and **8.1–8.5** (upgraded lessons).

## Hard rules
1. **Never delete or rewrite existing lesson content.** Upgrades are additive: use `_tools/upgrade_lesson.py` (`after_callout`, `before_heading`, `before_callout`, `at_end`, `set_meta`). Fix factual errors in place with a minimal edit only.
2. **Every number in a walkthrough must be computed, not guessed.** Run the maths in Python (option values via `figures/p8.bs()`), then write it.
3. **Facts that change over time** (prices, rates, index weights, company numbers, regulations, release times) must be researched, written with "as of <month year>" and kept out of evergreen explanations where possible. No buy/sell recommendations; add a `[!caution]` where money can be lost fast.
4. **Thai must mirror English completely.** Keep the English term in brackets on first use: *แนวรับ (Support)*.
5. **Times are given in UTC+7** with the northern-winter (+1h) note.
6. Figures: dark card style from `charts.py`; every text string goes through `t("en", "th")`; check that text doesn't overflow (render the SVG and look at it if you can).
7. After any change: `python3 _tools/make_figures.py <phase>` → `python3 _tools/build.py` → check there are no `BLOCKTOKEN` or `![[` strings left in `site/*.html` → update `_System/Lesson Audit.md` status table.
8. Work in **small batches** (one phase or 2–4 lessons at a time) and stop for the owner's review after each batch.

## Known gotchas
- `build.py` overwrites but never deletes files in `site/`; renamed lessons leave old pages behind.
- `sync.py` never overwrites an existing note; it only creates stubs.
- Lesson ids like `0.10` sort before `0.2` in Obsidian's file list; that's expected.
- Every lesson has `last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD` (shown on the site). Update it when you re-check a lesson.
- `upgrade_lesson.py` skips a block if a distinctive line (> 30 chars) from it already exists in that language section; make the first content line of each new block unique.
